items.q: What was Wendy actually shipping as the sole designer?
items.a: A 7,000-person conference on a 12–15 person team: **140+ sponsors, 300+ speakers, 600+ sessions**. Stickers, swag, landing pages, announcements, mascots, wayfinding, digital signage. Design team = Wendy + **Devin + GPT + Figma**.

items.q: What inspired the AI Engineer look?
items.a: The **scale problem**, not a moodboard. Tools are no longer the bottleneck. **Having a real problem is the advantage.**
**Foundation → reusable → automate → validate → remove friction.** Pin type/color so LLMs stop inventing font sizes. Website tokens let marketing rinse-repeat emails and flyers.

items.q: Pelican-on-a-bicycle SVG still fails. Then what?
items.a: Ask for a **PNG**, vectorize in Figma, ship. Work around jagged capability instead of waiting for native vectors.

items.q: How do room schedules get on the screens?
items.a: Devin **lives in Slack**. Pull latest data for a room/day, export **pixel-perfect PNG** to a flash drive. MCP or a Figma spec sheet (spacing/type/color, even on 'Frame 3') replaces the designer↔engineer loop.

items.q: How do you QA 140 logos and 300 headshots?
items.a: Ask Devin what is **missing** or **whether this photo is that speaker** (Tinder-style match). Wendy's logo test: **100%**. Human + AI is the QA team. The remaining job is **exceptions** — add the edit button the morning of.
